subject: starfish
subject_guess: Starfish (5-armed sea star), viewed from its aboral (top) side; body is radially symmetric with no distinct head
readings: Radially symmetric echinoderm: no head/neck exists, so 'profile' is not a single direction. The XY panel is the aboral PLAN view showing the full 5-arm star layout; z is the thin thickness/up-down axis of the flattened body.
Disc center read at (12,12) in XY panel (where all five arms converge).
Top arm tip at (12,0.5) in XY panel -> straight up from center, dx=0, screen dy=0.5-12=-11.5 => mesh dy=+11.5 (ascending, matches an arm pointing up-screen).
Left arm tip at (0.5,12) in XY panel -> dx=0.5-12=-11.5, dy=0 (level with center).
Right arm tip at (23,12) in XY panel -> dx=23-12=11, dy=0 (level with center).
Bottom-left arm tip at (8,23) in XY panel -> dx=8-12=-4, screen dy=23-12=11 => mesh dy=-11 (descending, matches arm going down-screen).
Bottom-right arm tip at (17,23) in XY panel -> dx=17-12=5, screen dy=11 => mesh dy=-11.
ZY panel: blade spans full y (0 to 24) with waist width z=8-16 around the middle, i.e. the top and bottom arms stay near z=12 (no lateral z offset) while the disc bulges the waist.
XZ panel: shape spans full x (0 to 24) with waist width z=8-16, i.e. the left/right arms stay near z=12 (no offset) while the central disc gives the raised bump seen at x=8-16.

All five arm lengths computed from center-to-tip distance are close to 12 grid units, consistent with a (near) 5-fold radial animal: top ~11.5, left ~11.5, right ~11, bottom-left ~11.7, bottom-right ~12.1.
notes: Subject is a 5-armed sea star (starfish) with radial (not bilateral) symmetry, so there is no head/neck and no single 'profile' panel in the usual sense; the XY panel is treated as the defining plan view since it alone shows all five arms and the central disc clearly. Z was inferred to be a thin thickness axis: the ZY and XZ panels each show only a narrow (z=8-16) waist because the arms lie essentially flat in the XY plane, and each panel's blade shape is really the SUM/overlap silhouette of whichever arms extend along that panel's vertical axis (y for ZY, x for XZ) - not a separate limb. Root is the central disc (length 0, direction [0,0,0]) per protocol. Each of the five arms is modeled as a single unsegmented flap/leaf, since sea-star arms have no internal joints, tapering smoothly from disc to tip; this single-segment choice is the only structural inference made. For the required symmetric-pair bookkeeping I treated the top arm as sitting on the animal's one bilateral axis (unpaired), and mirrored the remaining two left/right pairs (arm_L/arm_R and arm_BL/arm_BR) across that axis, which matches the near-identical lengths (~11-12 units) measured for all five arms. Lengths are the straight center-to-tip distances read off the XY panel, rounded to the nearest integer.
